paragraphs: Alexander's, Inc. (NYSE: ALX) is a real estate investment trust ("REIT"), incorporated in Delaware, engaged in leasing, managing, developing and redeveloping its properties. All references to "we," "us," "our," "Company" and "Alexander's" refer to Alexander's, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries. We are managed by, and our properties are leased and developed by, Vornado Realty Trust ("Vornado") (NYSE: VNO).
We have five properties in New York City consisting of:

•731 Lexington Avenue, a 1,080,000 square foot multi-use building, comprising the entire block bounded by Lexington Avenue, East 59th Street, Third Avenue and East 58th Street in Manhattan. The building contains 952,000 and 128,000 of rentable square feet of office and retail space, respectively. Bloomberg L.P. ("Bloomberg") occupies all of the office space. The Home Depot (83,000 square feet) was the principal retail tenant at the property until its lease expired on January 31, 2025;

•Rego Park II, a 606,000 square foot shopping center, is located on Junction Boulevard in Queens. The center is anchored by a 145,000 square foot Costco and a 133,000 square foot Kohl's. The center also includes a 60,000 square foot Burlington, a 47,000 square foot Best Buy, and a 40,000 square foot Marshalls. Kohl's' store is currently closed but the tenant remains obligated under its lease which expires in January 2031;
•Flushing, a 167,000 square foot building, located on Roosevelt Avenue and Main Street in Queens, that is subleased to New World Mall LLC. The property is ground leased through January 2037;

•Rego Park I, a 338,000 square foot shopping center, is located adjacent to our Rego Park II shopping center. The property is now vacant since the relocation of Burlington and Marshalls to Rego Park II in 2025. We are currently exploring sale opportunities for the property and are in advanced negotiations with a potential buyer; and
•The Alexander apartment tower, located above our Rego Park II shopping center, contains 312 units aggregating 255,000 square feet.

We are managed by, and our properties are leased and developed by, Vornado, pursuant to various agreements which expire in March of each year and are automatically renewable. Vornado is a fully-integrated REIT with significant experience in managing, leasing, developing, and operating office and retail properties.

As of December 31, 2025, Vornado owned 32.4% of our outstanding common stock. Steven Roth is the Chairman of our Board of Directors and Chief Executive Officer, the Managing General Partner of Interstate Properties ("Interstate"), a New Jersey general partnership, and the Chairman of the Board of Trustees and Chief Executive Officer of Vornado. As of December 31, 2025, Mr. Roth, Interstate and its other two general partners, David Mandelbaum and Russell B. Wight, Jr. (who are also directors of the Company and trustees of Vornado) owned, in the aggregate, 26.0% of our outstanding common stock, in addition to the 2.3% they indirectly own through Vornado.

Bloomberg accounted for revenue of $129,317,000, $125,349,000 and $120,351,000 in the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, representing approximately 61%, 55% and 54% of our rental revenues in each year, respectively. No other tenant accounted for more than 10% of our rental revenues. If we were to lose Bloomberg as a tenant, or if Bloomberg were to be unable to fulfill its obligations under its lease, it would adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition. In order to assist us in our continuing assessment of Bloomberg's creditworthiness, we receive certain confidential financial information and metrics from Bloomberg. In addition, we access and evaluate financial information regarding Bloomberg from other private sources, as well as publicly available data.

We have long believed a focus on environmental sustainability is responsible management of our business and important to our tenants, investors, employees and communities that we serve. Since we are externally managed by Vornado, Vornado's Corporate Governance and Nominating Committee of its Board of Trustees is assigned with oversight of sustainability matters at Alexander's, which includes climate change risk. Environmental sustainability initiatives are carried out by a dedicated team of professionals that work directly with Vornado's business units. In the discussion below, when we refer to Vornado's buildings, it includes our buildings.

Vornado is an industry leader in sustainability, owning and operating more than 26 million square feet of LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) certified buildings, representing 100% of its certifiable office portfolio, with over 24 million square feet at LEED Gold or Platinum. In 2025, Vornado:

•received GRESB's five star rating and an assessment score of 91, placing Vornado in the top 3% within the Americas/Listed category and the "Green Star" distinction for the thirteenth consecutive year; and
•achieved 100% WELL Health-Safety certification across its in-service office portfolio.

headings: We may be adversely affected by trends in office real estate.
All of our properties are in New York City and are affected by the economic cycles and risks inherent to this area.
We are subject to risks that affect the general and New York City retail environments.
Our performance and the value of an investment in us are subject to risks associated with our real estate assets and with the real estate industry.
Real estate is a competitive business and that competition may adversely impact us.
We may be unable to renew leases, lease vacant space or relet space as leases expire on favorable terms.
731 Lexington Avenue accounts for a majority of our revenues. Loss of or damage to the building would adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
Bloomberg represents a majority of our revenues. Loss of Bloomberg as a tenant or deterioration in Bloomberg's credit quality could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
Bankruptcy or insolvency of tenants may decrease our revenues, net income and available cash.
Some of our potential losses may not be covered by insurance.
Actual or threatened terrorist attacks or other criminal acts may adversely affect the value of our properties and our ability to generate cash flow.
The effects of climate change and natural disasters could have a concentrated impact on the area where we operate and could adversely impact our results.
Our properties are subject to transitional risks related to climate-related policy change.
Changes to tax laws could affect REITs generally, the trading of our shares and our results of operations, both positively and negatively, in ways that are difficult to anticipate.
Significant inflation and increases in the inflation rate could adversely affect our business and financial results.
We may acquire, develop, or redevelop properties and this may create risks.
We are exposed to risks associated with property development, redevelopment and repositioning that could adversely affect us, including our financial condition and results of operations.
It may be difficult to sell real estate on a timely basis, which may limit our flexibility.
Capital markets and economic conditions can materially affect our liquidity, financial condition and results of operations as well as the value of an investment in our common stock.
We have outstanding debt, and the amount of debt and its cost may increase; refinancing may not be available on acceptable terms and could affect our future operations.
Our existing financing documents contain covenants and restrictions that may restrict our operational and financial flexibility.
The hedge instruments we may use to manage our exposure to interest rate volatility involve risks.
Alexander's charter documents and applicable laws may hinder any attempt to acquire us.
We may change our policies without obtaining the approval of our stockholders.

Steven Roth, Vornado and Interstate may exercise substantial influence over us. They and some of our other directors and officers have interests or positions in other entities that may compete with us.
There may be conflicts of interest between Vornado, its affiliates and us.
The trading price of our common stock has been volatile and may continue to fluctuate.
Alexander's has additional shares of its common stock available for future issuance, which could decrease the market price of the common stock currently outstanding.
Loss of our key personnel could harm our operations and adversely affect the value of our common stock.
We may fail to qualify or remain qualified as a REIT, and may be required to pay federal income taxes at corporate rates, which could adversely impact the value of our common stock.
We may face possible adverse federal tax audits and changes in federal tax laws, which may result in an increase in our tax liability.
We may face possible adverse state and local tax audits and changes in state and local tax law.
Compliance or failure to comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act ("ADA") or other safety regulations and requirements could result in substantial costs.
We may incur significant costs to comply with environmental laws and environmental contamination may impair our ability to lease and/or sell real estate.
paragraphs: Material factors that may adversely affect our business, operations and financial condition are summarized below. The risks and uncertainties described herein may not be the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial may also adversely affect our business, operations and financial condition. See "Forward-Looking Statements" contained herein on page 4.
RISKS RELATED TO OUR BUSINESS AND OPERATIONS

In 2025, approximately 61% of our rental revenues was from Bloomberg, the office tenant at our 731 Lexington Avenue office property. Work from home, flexible or hybrid work schedules, open workplaces, videoconferencing, and teleconferencing have become more common in recent years. Changes in tenant space utilization, including from the continuation of work from home and flexible work arrangement policies, may cause office tenants to reassess their long-term physical space needs, which could have an adverse effect on our business. Additionally, the increased use of artificial intelligence ("AI") could result in changes in tenant space utilization, including the need to reduce or reconfigure space.

All of our revenues come from properties located in New York City. Real estate markets are affected by economic downturns and we cannot predict how economic conditions will impact the New York City market in either the short or long term. Declines in the economy and declines in the New York City real estate market have impacted and could impact our financial performance and the value of our properties. In addition to the factors affecting national economic conditions generally, the factors affecting economic conditions in this area include:
•financial performance and productivity of the media, advertising, professional services, financial, technology, retail, insurance and real estate industries;
•business layoffs or downsizing; •any oversupply of, or reduced demand for, real estate; •industry slowdowns;

paragraphs: Year Ended December 31, 2025 Financial Results Summary
Net income for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $28,224,000 or $5.50 per diluted share, compared to $43,444,000 or $8.46 per diluted share for the year ended December 31, 2024.

Funds from operations ("FFO") (non-GAAP) for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $62,995,000, or $12.27 per diluted share, compared to $77,968,000, or $15.19 per diluted share for the year ended December 31, 2024.
Square Footage, Occupancy and Leasing Activity
As of December 31, 2025, our portfolio was comprised of five properties aggregating 2,446,000 square feet. The commercial occupancy rate was 94.6% and the residential occupancy rate was 97.7%.
On January 31, 2025, Home Depot's 83,000 square foot lease at the retail portion of our 731 Lexington Avenue property expired. Annual rental revenues from Home Depot were approximately $15,000,000.

In the fourth quarter of 2024, we entered into ten-year leases with Burlington and Marshalls to relocate them to our Rego Park II property in 2025 from our Rego Park I property which is now vacant. We are currently exploring sale opportunities for our Rego Park I property and are in advanced negotiations with a potential buyer.

Bloomberg accounted for revenue of $129,317,000, $125,349,000 and $120,351,000 in the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, representing approximately 61%, 55% and 54% of our rental revenues in each year, respectively. No other tenant accounted for more than 10% of our rental revenues. If we were to lose Bloomberg as a tenant, or if Bloomberg were to be unable to fulfill its obligations under its lease, it would adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition. In order to assist us in our continuing assessment of Bloomberg's creditworthiness, we receive certain confidential financial information and metrics from Bloomberg. In addition, we access and evaluate financial information regarding Bloomberg from other private sources, as well as publicly available data.

On December 5, 2025, we completed a $175,000,000 refinancing of the mortgage loan on our Rego Park II shopping center. The interest-only loan is at SOFR plus 2.00% (5.72% as of December 31, 2025) and matures on December 5, 2030. We paid down by $23,544,000 the previous $198,544,000 loan that bore interest at SOFR plus 1.45% and was scheduled to mature on December 12, 2025.

On December 23, 2025, we entered into an agreement to restructure the $300,000,000 mortgage loan on the retail condominium portion of 731 Lexington Avenue, which previously bore interest at SOFR plus 1.51%. The restructured loan was split into (i) a $132,500,000 senior A-Note that was purchased by a wholly owned subsidiary of Alexander's, which bears interest at a fixed rate of 7.00% and (ii) a $167,500,000 junior C-Note held by the lenders of the original loan, which accrues PIK interest at 4.55%. In addition, Alexander's has the right to fund operating shortfalls, interest on the A-Note and capital for re-leasing at the property through a B-Note, which will be junior to the A-Note and senior to the C-Note. The B-Note bears interest at a fixed rate of 13.50%, except for loan amounts above $65,000,000 used to pay interest on the A-Note, which will bear interest at a fixed rate of 7.00%. The restructured loan matures in December 2035.

All future net sales or refinancing proceeds will be distributed through the payment waterfall per the terms of the restructured loan agreement. If such proceeds (or appraised value in such refinancing) are insufficient to cover the C-Note loan balance, any outstanding C-Note indebtedness that remains unpaid shall be forgiven.

Since the debt balances related to the A-Note and B-Note are eliminated in consolidation, the balance presented as mortgages payable for this loan on our consolidated balance sheet as of December 31, 2025 is $167,691,000, which is comprised of the principal balance of the C-Note and the PIK interest due upon maturity.

paragraphs: Alexander's, Inc. (紐約證券交易所：ALX) 為一間不動產投資信託（"REIT"），於特拉華州註冊成立，從事出租、管理、開發及重新開發其不動產。所有提及 "we," "us," "our," "Company" 及 "Alexander's" 皆指 Alexander's, Inc. 及其合併子公司。本公司由 Vornado Realty Trust ("Vornado") (紐約證券交易所：VNO) 管理，其不動產亦由 Vornado 租賃及開發。
本公司在紐約市共有五處不動產，包含：

•731 Lexington Avenue，為一間總計 1,080,000 平方英呎的多功能大樓，佔據曼哈頓 Lexington Avenue、East 59th Street、Third Avenue 及 East 58th Street 所圍成的整塊地。大樓內有 952,000 平方英呎的辦公空間及 128,000 平方英呎的零售空間。Bloomberg L.P. ("Bloomberg") 佔據全部辦公空間。The Home Depot (83,000 平方英呎) 曾為該不動產的主要零售租戶，直至其租約於 2025 年 1 月 31 日屆滿；

•Rego Park II，為一間總計 606,000 平方英呎的購物中心，位於皇后區 Junction Boulevard。該購物中心由一間 145,000 平方英呎的 Costco 及一間 133,000 平方英呎的 Kohl's 為主要租戶。該購物中心亦包含一間 60,000 平方英呎的 Burlington、一間 47,000 平方英呎的 Best Buy，以及一間 40,000 平方英呎的 Marshalls。Kohl's 的商店目前為關閉狀態，但租戶依其租約仍負有義務，租約於 2031 年 1 月屆滿；
•Flushing，為一間總計 167,000 平方英呎的建築物，位於皇后區 Roosevelt Avenue 及 Main Street。該不動產由 New World Mall LLC 進行次租賃。該不動產透過地租契約至 2037 年 1 月為止；
•Rego Park I，為一間總計 338,000 平方英呎的購物中心，位於本公司 Rego Park II 購物中心旁。該不動產自 2025 年 Burlington 及 Marshalls 移至 Rego Park II 後已閒置。本公司目前正探討出售機會，並與潛在買方進行進展中的談判；以及
•Alexander 公寓大樓，位於本公司 Rego Park II 購物中心之上，包含 312 個單位，總計 255,000 平方英呎。
本公司由 Vornado 管理，其不動產亦由 Vornado 租賃及開發，依據多項於每年 3 月屆滿且自動續約的契約。Vornado 為一間完整整合的 REIT，擁有豐富的經驗於管理、出租、開發及營運辦公及零售不動產。

截至2025年12月31日，Vornado持有我們流通普通股的32.4%。Steven Roth為我們董事會主席及首席執行官，為Interstate Properties（"Interstate"），一家新澤西州普通合夥企業的 managing general partner，同時為Vornado的董事會信託人主席及首席執行官。截至2025年12月31日，Roth先生、Interstate及其另外兩位普通合夥人David Mandelbaum與Russell B. Wight, Jr.（同時也是本公司董事及Vornado信託人）共同持有我們流通普通股的26.0%，另外透過Vornado間接持有2.3%。

Bloomberg 達成營業收入 129,317,000 美元、125,349,000 美元及 120,351,000 美元，分別為 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2023 年 12 月 31 日會計年度，分別約佔我們租賃收入的 61%、55% 及 54%。除 Bloomberg 以外，沒有其他租戶佔我們租賃收入超過 10%。若我們失去 Bloomberg 當租戶，或 Bloomberg 無法履行其租賃契約下的義務，將對我們的營運成果及財務狀況造成不利影響。為協助我們持續評估 Bloomberg 的信用worthiness，我們會收到 Bloomberg 提供的某些機密財務資訊及指標。此外，我們也會從其他私人來源取得並評估 Bloomberg 的財務資訊，以及公開可取得的資料。

我們長期認為，關注環境永續是對我們業務的負責任管理，並對我們的租戶、投資者、員工以及所服務的社區而言都非常重要。由於我們由Vornado外部管理，因此Vornado的董事會信託人企業治理與提名委員會負責監督Alexander's的永續發展事項，包括氣候變遷風險。環境永續發展計畫由專門的專業團隊執行，並直接與Vornado的業務單位合作。在以下討論中，當我們提及Vornado的建築物時，包括我們的建築物。
Vornado在永續發展領域為業界領導者，擁有並營運超過26 百萬平方英呎的LEED（Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design）認證建築物，佔其可認證辦公室資產的100%，其中超過24 百萬平方英呎達到LEED金級或白金級。在2025年，Vornado：
•獲得GRESB的五星評級與91分評估分數，使其在美洲/上市類別中排名前3%，並連續第十三年獲得"Green Star"稱號；且
•其營運中的辦公室資產已達成100% WELL Health-Safety認證。

paragraphs: 2025 年 12 月 31 日財務結果摘要
2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度淨收入為 28,224,000 美元，或每股稀釋後普通股 5.50 美元，與 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度淨收入 43,444,000 美元，或每股稀釋後普通股 8.46 美元相比。
2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度資金來自營運 ("FFO") (非 GAAP) 為 62,995,000 美元，或每股稀釋後普通股 12.27 美元，與 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度資金來自營運 ("FFO") (非 GAAP) 為 77,968,000 美元，或每股稀釋後普通股 15.19 美元相比。
樓地板面積、佔用率與租賃活動
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司資產組合包含五處不動產，總樓地板面積為 2,446,000 平方英呎。商業不動產佔用率為 94.6%，住宅不動產佔用率為 97.7%。
2025 年 1 月 31 日，Home Depot 在本公司 731 Lexington Avenue 不動產零售部分的 83,000 平方英呎租賃合約到期。來自 Home Depot 的年度租金收入約為 15,000,000 美元。
在 2024 年第四季，本公司與 Burlington 及 Marshalls 籤訂十年租賃合約，將其遷移至 2025 年本公司 Rego Park II 不動產，而非目前為空置的 Rego Park I 不動產。本公司目前正探討 Rego Park I 不動產的出售機會，且已與潛在買方進行進階談判。

Bloomberg 在 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度、2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度及 2023 年 12 月 31 日止年度分別產生 129,317,000 美元、125,349,000 美元及 120,351,000 美元的營業收入，分別佔本公司租金收入約 61%、55% 及 54%。其他租客未佔本公司租金收入 10% 以上。若 Bloomberg 無法作為租客，或無法履行其租賃契約義務，將對本公司營運結果與財務狀況造成不利影響。為協助本公司持續評估 Bloomberg 的信用狀況，本公司會接收 Bloomberg 提供的某些機密財務資訊與指標。此外，本公司也會從其他私人來源及公開資料評估 Bloomberg 的財務資訊。

於 2025 年 12 月 5 日，本公司完成對 Rego Park II 購物中心抵押貸款 175,000,000 美元的再融資。此筆貸款為僅付息貸款，利率為 SOFR 加 2.00%（截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日為 5.72%），並於 2030 年 12 月 5 日到期。本公司償還了先前 198,544,000 美元貸款中 23,544,000 美元，該貸款利率為 SOFR 加 1.45%，原定於 2025 年 12 月 12 日到期。

於 2025 年 12 月 23 日，本公司與電信業者簽訂協議，重新安排 731 Lexington Avenue 零售公寓部分的 300,000,000 美元抵押貸款，該貸款先前利率為 SOFR 加 1.51%。重新安排後的貸款分為 (i) 132,500,000 美元的 A-Note，由 Alexander's 的 wholly owned subsidiary 購買，利率為固定 7.00%；以及 (ii) 167,500,000 美元的 C-Note，由原貸款的貸款人持有，累積 PIK 利息為 4.55%。此外，Alexander's 有權透過 B-Note 資金補足營運虧損、A-Note 利息及重新出租的資本，該 B-Note 將優於 C-Note 且劣於 A-Note，利率為固定 13.50%，但用於支付 A-Note 利息的貸款金額超過 65,000,000 美元部分，利率為固定 7.00%。重新安排後的貸款於 2035 年 12 月到期。
所有未來的淨銷售額或再融資所得將依照重新安排貸款協議的條件，透過付款瀑布式分配。若此等所得（或再融資的評估價值）不足以覆蓋 C-Note 的貸款餘額，任何未償還的 C-Note 債務將被豁免。
由於 A-Note 和 B-Note 的債務在合併時已抵銷，本公司合併財務報表於 2025 年 12 月 31 日顯示的抵押貸款餘額為 167,691,000 美元，該餘額包含 C-Note 的本金及到期時應計的 PIK 利息。

headings: 我們可能因辦公室實體地產的趨勢而受到不利影響。
我們所有的不動產皆位於紐約市，並受此地區經濟週期及內在風險的影響。
我們面臨影響一般及紐約市零售環境的風險。
我們的營運表現及投資人對我們的投資價值，受我們不動產資產及不動產產業的相關風險影響。

與本公司業務及營運相關之風險

2025 年，本公司約 61% 的租金收入來自 Bloomberg，為本公司位於 731 Lexington Avenue 建築物之辦公租戶。近年來，遠端辦公、彈性或混合式工作排班、開放式辦公空間、視訊會議及電話會議已變得更加普遍。租戶空間使用率的變化，包括因遠端辦公及彈性工作安排政策持續進行，可能導致辦公租戶重新評估其長期實體空間需求，這可能會對本公司業務產生不利影響。此外，人工智慧（"AI"）使用率的增加，可能會導致租戶空間使用率的變化，包括減少或重新配置空間之需求。
本公司所有收入均來自紐約市之不動產。不動產市場受總體經濟衰退影響，本公司無法預測總體經濟狀況將如何影響紐約市市場，無論短期或長期。總體經濟衰退及紐約市不動產市場衰退已影響並可能繼續影響本公司之財務表現及不動產價值。除影響國家總體經濟狀況之因素外，影響本地區經濟狀況之因素包括：
• 媒體、廣告、專業服務、金融、科技、零售、保險及不動產行業之財務表現與生產力；
• 企業裁員或縮編人數；• 不動產供過於求，或需求減少；• 行業減速；
